time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 = t 0
units: pixels (x right, y down, full 1920x1080 resolution) and seconds; no metric scale

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the left tree-trunk strip vs frame 0: max shift < 0.02 px over all 60 frames (scene/scripts/bg.py)
camera.perspective: 2D side view; both elephants walk left-to-right parallel to the image plane on the same ground line (feet at y~693-695 for both), so one metres-per-pixel scale applies to both. Horizon / sea line y~640; grass edge y~690-700.

objects.name: elephant_big
objects.description: larger adult elephant, the one in front (right) walking right; grey-brown, large ears, curled trunk, tusks
objects.reference_point_recommended: centroid_x, centroid_y (mask centroid; proxy for the rig root/body centre)
objects.occlusion: none (in front of all trees); top edge lies against dark foliage, segmentation slightly less reliable there

objects.name: elephant_small
objects.description: smaller (juvenile / younger) elephant, behind (left of) the big one, walking right; tusks, trunk curled

objects.description: thick dark tree trunk at the far left foreground edge, full height of the upper image
objects.position_px: x ~65-205 (width ~140 px at y=500-650), from top of frame down to ground at y~720
